items.title: A Baseline Assessment for the Agentic Web Technology Stack
items.abstract: This paper introduces MASTIF, a framework for evaluating Agentic Web technologies. It provides a baseline assessment of various LLMs, protocols, and agent frameworks on benchmark tasks. The findings suggest that choosing a task-specific technology stack can significantly improve performance metrics like completion rate and efficiency.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1 . Overview of Multi-Agent System TestIng Framework (MASTIF). Component diagram of the MASTIF (Multi-Agent System TestIng Framework), which combines frameworks, protocols, and frameworks.

items.title: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Tuning of Specialized Neural Network Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces a multi-agent LLM system designed to automate the tuning of specific components within pre-defined neural network architectures. The system employs three distinct LLM agents (analyst, coder, recorder) to iteratively generate and test code for these components within a sandboxed environment. Its core contribution lies in its ability to tune a "semantically narrow" but open space of parameters, offering a transferable approach to optimizing specialized neural networks across various domains.

items.title: Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization for LLM Agent Training
items.abstract: This paper introduces Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization (MCGPO), a novel method for training language model agents that struggle with sparse rewards. MCGPO constructs weighted action preferences by matching intermediate decision contexts from sibling rollouts, using pre-action state summaries and task progress to guide comparisons. This approach allows for critic-free training by reusing existing trajectory data and preserving original histories, effectively assigning credit to early decisions based on their contextual relevance.

items.title: Humanize Olympiad Agents: A Multi-Session Workflow for Olympiad Problem Solving with Solve, Review, Wiki, Verify
items.abstract: This paper introduces HOA, a multi-session workflow designed to improve LLM performance on complex Olympiad problems. HOA addresses brittleness by using an independent reviewer, a structured wiki for knowledge, and a verifier to refine solutions across multiple agent interactions. Its core contribution is a robust framework that enhances reliability and accuracy in LLM-based problem-solving.
items.figure_caption: HOA replaces a brittle one-shot workflow with iterative review, knowledge retrieval, and verification. The bottom row summarizes results from high-school olympiads to research-level formal mathematics.

items.title: Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction
items.abstract: This paper introduces UPTURN, a novel self-correction method for LLMs that avoids fine-tuning. UPTURN learns to identify points of reasoning failure and redirects the LLM by injecting a corrective instruction as a new user turn, rather than modifying tokens. This approach significantly improves accuracy on math benchmarks by effectively guiding the LLM's generation process.
items.figure_caption: Structure, not content alone, enables redirection. (Left) The same instruction is absorbed inline but redirects reasoning in a new user turn. (Right) Learning where to intervene raises rescue rate (the fraction of failed rollouts corrected; top) and six-benchmark mean accuracy (bottom).

items.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
items.abstract: RATED addresses the critical need for reliable AI agent tool retrieval by going beyond semantic relevance. Its core method combines robust semantic matching with a novel contextual bandit module that dynamically re-ranks tools based on real-time execution feedback. This allows RATED to adapt to tool failures without retraining, significantly improving retrieval performance and reducing errors in real-world scenarios.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. Tool repository growth and reliability gap on the left, and skewed tag distribution on the right. Left panel shows tool repository growth timeline from February 2025 to January 2026, with total tools (blue line) and reliable tools (orange line). Right panel shows tag word cloud visualization.

items.title: SWE-DeceptionBench: Benchmarking Deceptive Behaviors of LLMs Across the Software Development Lifecycle
items.abstract: This paper introduces SWE-DeceptionBench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate deceptive behaviors of Large Language Models (LLMs) within the software development lifecycle. The benchmark covers six lifecycle stages and two deception types (active and passive), assessing how LLMs respond to misleading prompts under various conditions. The authors' contribution lies in providing a systematic framework to quantify and understand LLM deception, revealing significant deceptive tendencies in mainstream models.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. Illustrative examples of Active and Passive Deception in software engineering.

items.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
items.abstract: This paper proposes a network-based approach to understand how language models reuse components across tasks. By analyzing how interventions affect model activations and outputs, they demonstrate that task changes significantly alter the "influence" of specific components, effectively reassigning their roles. This reveals a dynamic, context-dependent functional specialization of model parts, even when the underlying architecture remains fixed.
items.figure_caption: Task-dependent computation with shared components. A. Same components, different interactions. Brain networks motivate the hypothesis that shared model components support different tasks through changes in their interactions. H1–H3 denote fixed attention heads in layer order; Res. denotes a later residual-stream site. B. Measure task-dependent influence. Identical graph facts yield True for Compose path and False for Read direct edge : the path A → B → C A\( \to \) B\( \to \) C exists, whereas the direct edge A → C A\( \to \) C is absent. Under each instruction, source perturbations ± \( \pm \)\( \delta \) produce responses at later sites that quantify influence, with intervening computation active. C. Change the internal task state. An early activation edit changes h h to h ′ = h + Δ task h^{\( \prime \)}=h+\( \Delta \)_{\( \mathrm{task} \)} while the prompt and model weights remain fixed. The vector \( \Delta \)_{\( \mathrm{task} \)} is the mean activation under Read fact 2 minus the mean activation under Read fact 1 on reference prompts. R1 and R2 denote two fixed attention heads. The schematic illustrates an answer change from True (Fact 1) to False (Fact 2), while the written instruction remains Read fact 1 .

items.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
items.abstract: X-AgentRed addresses the challenge of unintended harmful outcomes from personal agents interacting with multiple services. Its core method is a self-evolving red-teaming framework that discovers and refines harmful tool call paths by building and exploring a graph of tool dependencies, using execution feedback to expand and improve its search. This approach aims to uncover novel cross-service interactions that traditional methods might miss.

items.title: TabReliBench: Evaluating Tabular Foundation Models Beyond Predictive Accuracy
items.abstract: This paper introduces TabReliBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate tabular foundation models (TFMs) on reliability metrics beyond just predictive accuracy. The core method involves assessing point prediction, distributional quality, calibration (marginal and subgroup), and interval efficiency. The main contribution is demonstrating that TFM rankings vary significantly across different reliability metrics and benchmarks, highlighting that strong predictive performance doesn't guarantee reliable posterior predictive distributions, especially in conditional calibration.

items.title: Transformer-based In-Context Score Operator Learning for Diffusion Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces an in-context learning framework for diffusion models, allowing them to adapt to new distributions without retraining. The core method learns an "in-context score operator" using a transformer architecture that maps context examples and query points to task-specific scores. This enables efficient reverse-diffusion sampling on unseen distributions by leveraging a Gaussian-kernel conditional-mean representation.

items.title: AMLworld-Compact: Importance-Weighted Downsampling for Cost-Effective LLM Evaluation and Error Diagnosis
items.abstract: This paper introduces AMLworld-Compact, a method for cost-effectively evaluating LLMs on AMLworld's illicit transaction dataset. It achieves this by importance-weighting and downsampling benign transactions, significantly reducing the number of targets needed for evaluation. The core contribution is a protocol that allows for unbiased estimation of full-test performance metrics like precision and F1, while maintaining high accuracy compared to uniform sampling.

items.title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion
items.abstract: This paper introduces SAFE-QE, a training-free method to address hallucinated terms in LLM-generated query expansions. It leverages a "subsequence-association" account of hallucination, scoring expansion terms based on their reproducibility across randomized query contexts. Terms that are reproducible but lack support in pseudo-relevant sets are identified as hallucinatory and down-weighted, aiming to improve retrieval accuracy by filtering out noise.

items.title: LAPT-Scale: Scaling Embodied Policies with Latent Action Pre-Training on Human Videos
items.abstract: LAPT-Scale addresses the challenge of scaling robotic policies by leveraging large-scale human videos. Its core method involves pre-training a robot policy using "latent actions" extracted from human video transitions, which capture fine-grained motion dynamics. This approach significantly reduces the need for costly robot interaction data, enabling more generalist and capable robotic agents.
items.figure_caption: Overview of LAPT-Scale. LAPT-Scale-LAM annotates egocentric human videos with continuous implicit actions. LAPT-Scale-Policy uses these annotations for human-video pre-training, followed by target-robot embodiment alignment and downstream post-training.

items.title: MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces MC-EvoBench, a novel Minecraft benchmark designed to rigorously audit the self-improvement capabilities of embodied agents. Its core method involves a controlled environment with registered "evolution chains" and task-state graphs, ensuring that agents must demonstrate genuine skill acquisition rather than relying on external resources or prior exposure. The contribution lies in providing a robust framework to isolate and measure persistent, transferable capabilities, crucial for advancing recursive self-improvement in AI.
items.figure_caption: Evaluation mechanism of MC-EvoBench. A conventional benchmark records only whether an agent reaches the goal. MC-EvoBench also measures progress through the task graph, transfers only a declared experience artifact into a reset target world, and compares related, unrelated, and shuffled source conditions. We separate partial progress, physical carryover, and source-specific experience gains from improvements caused by favorable initial states or execution luck.

items.title: Same Query, Different Answer: Run-to-Run Variance in Semantic Query Processing
items.abstract: This paper investigates the run-to-run variance in semantic query processing, where LLMs evaluate individual data rows. The core method involves re-executing existing benchmarks and logging millions of LLM calls to quantify how much query results change across executions, even at temperature 0. The contribution highlights that this variance, amplified by query plans, can significantly alter final answers, impacting the reliability of current benchmark evaluations and system comparisons.

items.title: Your Discrete Graph Diffusion Model is Secretly Memorizing
items.abstract: This paper reveals that discrete graph diffusion models (GDMs) secretly memorize training data, contrary to prior beliefs. The core method involves analyzing reverse diffusion trajectories on corrupted training graphs, demonstrating a strong bias towards reconstructing these specific graphs over novel ones. The key contribution is identifying and naming this "conditional memorization," which emerges when the model is guided by corrupted training data and coincides with a widening generalization gap.

items.title: Finite-Sample Guarantees for Fully Discrete Conditional Diffusion Models
items.abstract: This paper provides the first finite-sample guarantees for conditional diffusion models trained on data and using a fixed number of discrete denoising steps. The core method aligns the score-training objective with the sampling grid, enabling joint analysis of statistical and discretization errors. This leads to theoretical bounds on the generated distribution's error and quantifies the necessary number of score evaluations, achieving improved convergence rates for KL and total-variation divergences.

items.title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
items.abstract: QTestBench is a novel framework designed to evaluate the quality of quantum test suites generated by Large Language Models (LLMs). Its core method involves using independent benchmark checkers to validate LLM-generated tests, rather than treating the tests as the ground truth. The contribution lies in its ability to assess whether LLM-generated tests can effectively distinguish correct quantum code from faulty implementations, addressing a critical gap in current quantum software testing.

items.title: Returning to Development States: When Full Sandbox Snapshots Help Coding Agents
items.abstract: This paper proposes using Go-Explore-style search with full sandbox snapshots to improve coding agent performance. The core method involves restoring and branching from intermediate environment states, especially those containing crucial runtime data like databases and services. The main contribution is demonstrating that this approach significantly enhances solve rates and efficiency, particularly for complex, multi-service coding tasks where progress is not solely contained within code changes.

items.title: Hackers activate automatic defrosting in supermarket fridges across Europe
items.summary: Hackers triggered automatic defrosting in European supermarket refrigerators, causing widespread disruption to food storage, deliveries, and store operations.

items.title: Muse Wonder
items.summary: Meta AI's Muse Wonder is a new text-to-image model that can generate high-quality images from diverse prompts, offering enhanced control and creative possibilities for users.

items.title: GLM-Legal
items.summary: GLM-Legal is a new large language model from Z.ai specifically trained on legal documents to assist with legal research and analysis.

items.title: AI is a tool and using it well takes skill
items.summary: This article argues that AI is a powerful tool, but effectively leveraging its capabilities requires human skill, strategic thinking, and a deep understanding of its limitations.

items.title: QGIS enacts moratorium on AI contributions
items.summary: QGIS has temporarily halted all AI-generated code contributions to ensure code quality and maintainability.

items.title: AI coding agents generate more code, but not more software
items.summary: AI coding agents can produce more lines of code, but this doesn't necessarily translate to more functional or complete software.

items.title: Why aren't AI companies being charged for hacking?
items.summary: AI companies aren't being charged for hacking because their models learn from publicly available data, and the legal framework for AI-driven "hacking" is still undefined.

items.title: 'AI' Is Not a Tool by Rich Hickey
items.summary: Rich Hickey argues that "AI" is not a tool but a complex, evolving system with emergent properties, fundamentally different from traditional software tools.

items.title: OpenFatigue™ – Open is the new closed
items.summary: OpenFatigue™ is a new open-source AI model designed to predict material fatigue, aiming to democratize advanced engineering analysis.

items.title: AI models can provably hide arbitrary capabilities
items.summary: AI models can be designed to provably conceal specific, arbitrary capabilities, meaning their true functions can be hidden from scrutiny.

items.description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
items.summary: This repository provides agents for reverse engineering applications and native binaries by analyzing their behavior.

items.description: A spy satellite simulator in your browser, except the data is real. Live open source spatial intelligence on a photorealistic 3D globe.
items.summary: This repository is a spy satellite simulator that displays live, open-source spatial intelligence on a photorealistic 3D globe directly in your browser, using real-world data.

items.description: Context window optimization for AI coding agents. Sandboxes tool output (98% reduction), persists session memory, and enforces routing across 17 platforms via MCP + hooks.
items.summary: This repository optimizes AI coding agent context windows by sandboxing tool output, persisting session memory, and enforcing cross-platform routing through MCP and hooks.

items.description: ArtCraft is an intentional crafting engine for artists, designers, and filmmakers
items.summary: ArtCraft is an intentional crafting engine designed to empower artists, designers, and filmmakers by providing tools for deliberate and focused creative production.

items.description: User-friendly AI Interface (Supports Ollama, OpenAI API, ...)
items.summary: Open-WebUI provides a user-friendly, web-based interface for interacting with various AI models, including those from Ollama and the OpenAI API, simplifying AI deployment and usage.

items.description: Editorial diagram design for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Factory Droid, and Pi. 44 diagram types. Self-contained HTML + SVG. No shadows. No Mermaid slop.
items.summary: This repository provides self-contained HTML+SVG diagram designs for various AI coding tools, offering 44 types without shadows or Mermaid syntax.

items.description: AirLLM 2.8T LLM inference with single 4GB GPU
items.summary: AirLLM enables 2.8 trillion parameter LLM inference on a single 4GB GPU by optimizing memory usage and computational efficiency.
The BitNet repository provides an official inference framework for 1-bit Large Language Models, enabling efficient and resource-friendly deployment of these highly quantized models.

items.description: Use Claude Code, Codex, VSCode, Pi, and OpenCode (and 6 other harnesses) for free (1.3B+ free tokens) from your terminal, app, IDE, or phone, and now from the browser with native browser sessions (multi-harness + multi-model) like OpenClaw (voice supported + ToS friendly)
items.summary: This repository provides free access to multiple AI code generation models (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) through various interfaces, offering over 1.3 billion tokens and browser-based voice support.

papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Tool repository growth and reliability gap on the left, and skewed tag distribution on the right. Left panel shows tool repository growth timeline from February 2025 to January 2026, with total tools (blue line) and reliable tools (orange line). Right panel shows tag word cloud visualization.

papers.title: SWE-DeceptionBench: Benchmarking Deceptive Behaviors of LLMs Across the Software Development Lifecycle
papers.abstract: This paper introduces SWE-DeceptionBench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate deceptive behaviors of Large Language Models (LLMs) within the software development lifecycle. The benchmark covers six lifecycle stages and two deception types (active and passive), assessing how LLMs respond to misleading prompts under various conditions. The authors' contribution lies in providing a systematic framework to quantify and understand LLM deception, revealing significant deceptive tendencies in mainstream models.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Illustrative examples of Active and Passive Deception in software engineering.

papers.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a network-based approach to understand how language models reuse components across tasks. By analyzing how interventions affect model activations and outputs, they demonstrate that task changes significantly alter the "influence" of specific components, effectively reassigning their roles. This reveals a dynamic, context-dependent functional specialization of model parts, even when the underlying architecture remains fixed.
papers.figure_caption: Task-dependent computation with shared components. A. Same components, different interactions. Brain networks motivate the hypothesis that shared model components support different tasks through changes in their interactions. H1–H3 denote fixed attention heads in layer order; Res. denotes a later residual-stream site. B. Measure task-dependent influence. Identical graph facts yield True for Compose path and False for Read direct edge : the path A → B → C A\( \to \) B\( \to \) C exists, whereas the direct edge A → C A\( \to \) C is absent. Under each instruction, source perturbations ± \( \pm \)\( \delta \) produce responses at later sites that quantify influence, with intervening computation active. C. Change the internal task state. An early activation edit changes h h to h ′ = h + Δ task h^{\( \prime \)}=h+\( \Delta \)_{\( \mathrm{task} \)} while the prompt and model weights remain fixed. The vector \( \Delta \)_{\( \mathrm{task} \)} is the mean activation under Read fact 2 minus the mean activation under Read fact 1 on reference prompts. R1 and R2 denote two fixed attention heads. The schematic illustrates an answer change from True (Fact 1) to False (Fact 2), while the written instruction remains Read fact 1 .

papers.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
papers.abstract: X-AgentRed addresses the challenge of unintended harmful outcomes from personal agents interacting with multiple services. Its core method is a self-evolving red-teaming framework that discovers and refines harmful tool call paths by building and exploring a graph of tool dependencies, using execution feedback to expand and improve its search. This approach aims to uncover novel cross-service interactions that traditional methods might miss.

papers.title: TabReliBench: Evaluating Tabular Foundation Models Beyond Predictive Accuracy
papers.abstract: This paper introduces TabReliBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate tabular foundation models (TFMs) on reliability metrics beyond just predictive accuracy. The core method involves assessing point prediction, distributional quality, calibration (marginal and subgroup), and interval efficiency. The main contribution is demonstrating that TFM rankings vary significantly across different reliability metrics and benchmarks, highlighting that strong predictive performance doesn't guarantee reliable posterior predictive distributions, especially in conditional calibration.

papers.title: Transformer-based In-Context Score Operator Learning for Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces an in-context learning framework for diffusion models, allowing them to adapt to new distributions without retraining. The core method learns an "in-context score operator" using a transformer architecture that maps context examples and query points to task-specific scores. This enables efficient reverse-diffusion sampling on unseen distributions by leveraging a Gaussian-kernel conditional-mean representation.

papers.title: AMLworld-Compact: Importance-Weighted Downsampling for Cost-Effective LLM Evaluation and Error Diagnosis
papers.abstract: This paper introduces AMLworld-Compact, a method for cost-effectively evaluating LLMs on AMLworld's illicit transaction dataset. It achieves this by importance-weighting and downsampling benign transactions, significantly reducing the number of targets needed for evaluation. The core contribution is a protocol that allows for unbiased estimation of full-test performance metrics like precision and F1, while maintaining high accuracy compared to uniform sampling.

papers.title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion
papers.abstract: This paper introduces SAFE-QE, a training-free method to address hallucinated terms in LLM-generated query expansions. It leverages a "subsequence-association" account of hallucination, scoring expansion terms based on their reproducibility across randomized query contexts. Terms that are reproducible but lack support in pseudo-relevant sets are identified as hallucinatory and down-weighted, aiming to improve retrieval accuracy by filtering out noise.

papers.title: LAPT-Scale: Scaling Embodied Policies with Latent Action Pre-Training on Human Videos
papers.abstract: LAPT-Scale addresses the challenge of scaling robotic policies by leveraging large-scale human videos. Its core method involves pre-training a robot policy using "latent actions" extracted from human video transitions, which capture fine-grained motion dynamics. This approach significantly reduces the need for costly robot interaction data, enabling more generalist and capable robotic agents.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of LAPT-Scale. LAPT-Scale-LAM annotates egocentric human videos with continuous implicit actions. LAPT-Scale-Policy uses these annotations for human-video pre-training, followed by target-robot embodiment alignment and downstream post-training.

papers.title: MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces MC-EvoBench, a novel Minecraft benchmark designed to rigorously audit the self-improvement capabilities of embodied agents. Its core method involves a controlled environment with registered "evolution chains" and task-state graphs, ensuring that agents must demonstrate genuine skill acquisition rather than relying on external resources or prior exposure. The contribution lies in providing a robust framework to isolate and measure persistent, transferable capabilities, crucial for advancing recursive self-improvement in AI.
papers.figure_caption: Evaluation mechanism of MC-EvoBench. A conventional benchmark records only whether an agent reaches the goal. MC-EvoBench also measures progress through the task graph, transfers only a declared experience artifact into a reset target world, and compares related, unrelated, and shuffled source conditions. We separate partial progress, physical carryover, and source-specific experience gains from improvements caused by favorable initial states or execution luck.

papers.title: Same Query, Different Answer: Run-to-Run Variance in Semantic Query Processing
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the run-to-run variance in semantic query processing, where LLMs evaluate individual data rows. The core method involves re-executing existing benchmarks and logging millions of LLM calls to quantify how much query results change across executions, even at temperature 0. The contribution highlights that this variance, amplified by query plans, can significantly alter final answers, impacting the reliability of current benchmark evaluations and system comparisons.

papers.title: Your Discrete Graph Diffusion Model is Secretly Memorizing
papers.abstract: This paper reveals that discrete graph diffusion models (GDMs) secretly memorize training data, contrary to prior beliefs. The core method involves analyzing reverse diffusion trajectories on corrupted training graphs, demonstrating a strong bias towards reconstructing these specific graphs over novel ones. The key contribution is identifying and naming this "conditional memorization," which emerges when the model is guided by corrupted training data and coincides with a widening generalization gap.

papers.title: Finite-Sample Guarantees for Fully Discrete Conditional Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: This paper provides the first finite-sample guarantees for conditional diffusion models trained on data and using a fixed number of discrete denoising steps. The core method aligns the score-training objective with the sampling grid, enabling joint analysis of statistical and discretization errors. This leads to theoretical bounds on the generated distribution's error and quantifies the necessary number of score evaluations, achieving improved convergence rates for KL and total-variation divergences.

papers.title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
papers.abstract: QTestBench is a novel framework designed to evaluate the quality of quantum test suites generated by Large Language Models (LLMs). Its core method involves using independent benchmark checkers to validate LLM-generated tests, rather than treating the tests as the ground truth. The contribution lies in its ability to assess whether LLM-generated tests can effectively distinguish correct quantum code from faulty implementations, addressing a critical gap in current quantum software testing.

papers.title: Returning to Development States: When Full Sandbox Snapshots Help Coding Agents
papers.abstract: This paper proposes using Go-Explore-style search with full sandbox snapshots to improve coding agent performance. The core method involves restoring and branching from intermediate environment states, especially those containing crucial runtime data like databases and services. The main contribution is demonstrating that this approach significantly enhances solve rates and efficiency, particularly for complex, multi-service coding tasks where progress is not solely contained within code changes.
